children: China's blue-chip shares edged lower on Friday and were headed for a 12th consecutive weekly loss, as a global selloff in AI stocks weighed on sentiment, though Hong Kong-listed internet companies bucked the trend.
** China's blue-chip CSI300 Index
dropped 0.4% to a one-year low by the lunch break, while the Shanghai Composite Index
lost 0.3%. Hong Kong benchmark Hang Seng
was up 1.6%.

** The CSI300 Index was down 0.9% for the week and 7.6% for the month, and on track for its biggest monthly loss since July. Over the last 12 weeks, it has lost 14%, the longest losing streak on record.
** The Hang Seng Index was up 1.1% this week.
** AI-related shares led declines onshore following overnight declines in New York and along with their Asian peers. Shares in Google parent Alphabet
, Amazon.com
and Intel
all fell on AI cash burn. Memory chip giant SK Hynix
fell more than 7%.
** Shanghai's tech-focused STAR50 index
fell 1.8%.
** CSI 5G communications
, a gauge that measures the industry, plunged as much as 6% in early trade. Shares of Chinese optical module producer Eoptolink Tech
tumbled nearly 8% and were down 46% this month.
** Against broad declines, consumer staple shares
rose 1%.
** Tech majors listed in Hong Kong
rebounded, up 1.4%, although the gauge still hovers near its lowest level in two years.

** "At valuations of 10-11 times price-to-earnings after accounting for new AI investment, we think some stocks are increasingly treating the spending peak as a permanent earnings burden, while assigning limited value to a normalisation of future cash flows or successful AI monetisation," said Kenneth Fong, head of China internet research at UBS.
** Mainland property developers in Hong Kong
rose 2.7%.
